description: Synthetic stand-in certificates for the TLS trust decision (#68). The leaf carries the live relay's captured P-256 public key from relay-spki-pin.json (forced in with -force_pubkey), so its SPKI pin is the relay's published pin, but it is not the relay's certificate: it is issued by a throwaway P-256 issuer whose private key was deleted after signing, as were the P-384 and RSA leaf keys. Every pin here was computed by openssl as base64 SHA-256 over DER, independently of the code under test. Certificates are base64 DER.
source: generated 2026-10-15 with OpenSSL 4.0.3 29 Sep 2026 (Library: OpenSSL 4.0.3 29 Sep 2026), in a scratch directory; every private key deleted afterwards
openssl x509 -new -subj /CN=dsh-relay-stand-in -force_pubkey relay-pub.pem -CA issuer.pem -CAkey issuer.key -days 3650 -set_serial 2 -out leaf.pem
openssl genpkey -algorithm EC -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-384 -out p384.key; openssl pkey -in p384.key -pubout -out p384-pub.pem
openssl x509 -new -subj /CN=dsh-test-p384-leaf -force_pubkey p384-pub.pem -CA issuer.pem -CAkey issuer.key -days 3650 -set_serial 3 -out p384.pem
openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048 -out rsa.key; openssl pkey -in rsa.key -pubout -out rsa-pub.pem
openssl x509 -new -subj /CN=dsh-test-rsa-leaf -force_pubkey rsa-pub.pem -CA issuer.pem -CAkey issuer.key -days 3650 -set_serial 4 -out rsa.pem
SPKI pin: openssl x509 -in X.pem -pubkey -noout | openssl pkey -pubin -outform DER | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | base64
whole-certificate pin: openssl x509 -in X.pem -outform DER | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | base64
